name: "Weird Al" Yankovic
hook: A song parodist whose band re-records a hit's arrangement as closely as it can while he changes the words, usually with the original artist's blessing, which makes his catalogue a record of which songs everyone knew.
blurb: Alfred Yankovic was born in Downey, California, in 1959 and had his first accordion lesson the day before he turned seven. He got his start through Dr. Demento, a radio DJ whose comedy show was broadcast across the country, who first played one of Yankovic's home-made tapes in 1976, when he was 16. In 1979 he recorded 'My Bologna', a joke version of the Knack's 'My Sharona', on his accordion in a restroom across from his college radio station, because the echo sounded good, and Capitol put it out as a single. His method has stayed the same: his parodies keep the music of a hit song, played by his band to sound as close to the original as they can, and change the words, and he asks the original artist for permission first. Rick Derringer produced his records from his first album, on Scotti Brothers in 1983, until Yankovic took over in 1992. 'Eat It' (1984), his parody of Michael Jackson's 'Beat It', from 'In 3-D', reached number 12 in America, his first top 40 hit, and won the Grammy for Best Comedy Recording. The same album had 'Polkas on 45', a string of hit songs by Devo, Deep Purple, Berlin, the Beatles and others played as fast accordion polkas, and most of his albums since have had a polka medley of about a dozen current songs. He is on this map because a parody only works if you already know the song, so his records show which songs were big enough for everyone to know, and several of them are close studies of other people's arrangements.

signatureTracks.title: My Bologna
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The first release: a Knack parody on solo accordion, recorded in a restroom for the echo.

signatureTracks.title: Eat It
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The breakthrough, and the clearest example of the method: Michael Jackson's arrangement rebuilt closely, with new words.

signatureTracks.title: The Hot Rocks Polka
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Twelve Rolling Stones songs turned into one continuous accordion polka.
